notes: Platform is a terminal: sizes are cells (1 col x 1 row) and half-block pixels (2 px per row). No CSS radius or shadow exists in the build.

Hex values are copied exactly from src/app/theme.ts (K), src/app/stage/theme.ts (T), src/grid/color.ts and packages/pixel/src/palette.ts. The feature renderers (src/app/features/*.ts) draw with K tokens, not literals. No tonal ramps are given: the source defines none, and synthesising them would invent colours.
Captures (.impeccable/review/*.png) are rendered at 9x18 px per cell, 15 px font: phone 40x52, laptop 100x32, wide 160x44 cells.
T.panel #0d1319 is declared in src/app/stage/theme.ts but never drawn; it is not a token.

decisions.name: No owner emoji

decisions.name: Local time

decisions.name: 8 fps clock
decisions.body: The animation clock is 8 fps on a 125 ms grid and renders only when a displayed frame changes.

decisions.name: Ten and six

narrative.overview: Porch is an arcade cabinet switched on in a dark room. The ground is near-black glass with a scanline on every odd row. The crew stand on a stage as pixel characters, and the conversation runs underneath in plain mixed-case text. Every surface is drawn in terminal cells. All art is drawn in half blocks, which pack two full-colour pixels into each cell. Box-drawing frames, block-element rules and bold words do the work that borders, shadows and buttons do elsewhere. Colour follows a state law inherited from Loom, and the law never relaxes: cyan is Trey and only Trey, green is engaged or ready, magenta is where an agent is headed, red is warning, power gold means signed and verified and nothing else, and caution is a word and a dotted frame, never amber. Nothing moves unless a finite burst is running.
keyCharacteristics: Glass ground (glass) with odd-row scanlines (scan). Chrome sits on raised bezel bars.
Half-block pixel art for every sprite, head, title and plate. █ is never emitted.
A 3x5 pixel-caps display font for titles and big moments. Everything else is one terminal monospace.
A strict colour law (cyan, green, magenta, red, gold) with a word or glyph on every state.
Bursts on a 125 ms grid. Idle draws nothing.
Phone (40 cols), laptop (100 cols) and wide (160 cols) are all first-class.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Each signal colour means one thing everywhere: cyan is Trey, green is ready, magenta is headed, red is warning, gold is verified.

rules.name: The Gold Is Earned Rule
rules.body: Gold appears only for a signed send that verified: the ✓ SIGNED chip and the SIGNED! plate.

rules.name: The Caution Is A Word Rule
rules.body: Caution is CAUTION · on bezel-hi, or ? UNVERIFIED in a dotted frame. There is no amber.

rules.name: The Word Behind Every Colour Rule
rules.body: Every state has a word or glyph, so NO_COLOR keeps every meaning.

rules.name: The NO_COLOR Underline Rule
rules.body: Under NO_COLOR every chip and lit bar draws as bold underlined words in its colour; the red ✗ SIGNATURE FAILED banner is the single reverse-video exception.

rules.name: The One Size Rule
rules.body: All text is one cell tall. Big type is always the pixel font.

rules.name: The Plain Words Rule
rules.body: Message bodies are normal mixed-case text, never the pixel font, never upper-cased.

rules.name: The Whole Record Rule
rules.body: The stage floor cuts the stream only at a message boundary; a record whose first row would sit above it is left out whole.

rules.name: The Ten-and-Six Rule
rules.body: Stage strips are 10 rows for bodies and 6 for heads; message heads are 8x8 pixels.

rules.name: The Flat Glass Rule
rules.body: Raise a surface with bezel fills and half-block lips, or frame it with box drawing. Never fake a shadow.

rules.name: The No Emoji Rule
rules.body: The score bar draws no owner emoji; Porch never draws an emoji as art.

rules.name: The Machinery Off Stage Rule
rules.body: Polls and ballots never reach the stage task line.

rules.name: The Body-Only Plug-in Rule
rules.body: Core draws head, sender line, badge and reply line; plug-in renderers draw the body only.

rules.name: The One Line Ballot Rule
rules.body: An unframed ballot is one undimmed line of plain words: <Name> voted A on p1. A framed ballot (unverified or failed) uses the same words, in gray and never dimmed, as its body.

dos: Do route every new chip or lit bar through chip() so NO_COLOR draws it as bold underlined words.
Do give every state a word or glyph alongside its colour.
Do draw art as half blocks from the sprite palette, and redraw it as line work or dither under NO_COLOR.
Do keep message bodies in plain mixed-case data text. Put arcade voice in chrome, titles and moments.
Do make every animation a finite burst on the 125 ms grid, with a reduced-motion end state.
Do keep the 10-col gutter and the 8x8 head at every width, phone included.
Do cut the stream at record boundaries only.
donts: Don't use gold for anything but a verified signature and its SIGNED! plate.
Don't use cyan for anyone but Trey, or let an agent accent resolve to cyan, lemon or red.
Don't use amber for caution. Use the word and the dotted frame.
Don't draw a solid white or light block: no █, and no lit bar under NO_COLOR except the failure banner.
Don't give the reverse-video exception to any state other than ✗ SIGNATURE FAILED.
Don't draw an emoji as art (no owner emoji in the score bar), or show a raw ballot.
Don't let a plug-in renderer draw a head, header, badge or reply line.
Don't run a timer that draws when nothing is moving.
Don't use gray-dim for text that must be read. It is for rules, leaders, the no-task dash and the away/unknown presence glyph beside its word.
